title: SonicWall warns of unpatched flaws in end-of-life GMS software
content_md: SonicWall warned customers of two security flaws affecting end-of-life Global Management System (GMS) systems that will not be patched. Global Management System (GMS) helps IT admins deploy and manage thousands of SonicWall security appliances from a single interface, but SonicWall has officially replaced it with the Network Security Manager (NSM) management platform. The two vulnerabilities were found and reported by Pentest-Tools security researchers and affect systems running SonicWall GMS 9.5.2 and earlier. The first GMS flaw disclosed this week is tracked as CVE-2026-109593 , and it enables unauthenticated attackers with network access to vulnerable instances (running GMS 9.5.2 and earlier versions) to steal sensitive information by reading internal files. SonicWall also flagged a second security issue ( CVE-2026-109594 ) that can let threat actors with high privileges access or modify information stored in the GMS database through low-complexity SQL Injection attacks. On Tuesday, SonicWall also urged customers to upgrade to NMS, as it will not release security patches because the vulnerable systems have now reached end of life. "The affected product has reached End-of-Life (EOL). As a result, no remediation or security update will be released for these vulnerabilities," SonicWall warned on Tuesday. "Organizations using the product should be aware of the associated security risks and are strongly encouraged to upgrade to the SonicWall Network Security Manager (NSM)." Att
